angular-momentum-quant.name: Angular Momentum (L = n·ℏ)
angular-momentum-quant.intro: Compute the orbital angular momentum of an electron from the principal quantum number n using the simplified L = n·ℏ relation, useful for atomic-physics and quantum-mechanics exercises.

band-gap-photon.name: Band-Gap Photon Wavelength
band-gap-photon.intro: Enter the band-gap energy E_g (eV) of a semiconductor or material and compute the corresponding absorbed or emitted photon wavelength (nm) via λ = hc/E_g, to judge emitted color or excitable wavelength.

bohr-orbit-radius.name: Bohr Orbit Radius
bohr-orbit-radius.intro: Compute the radius of the n-th hydrogen orbit (an integer-square multiple of the Bohr radius), suitable for atomic-structure models and quantum-physics teaching demos.

boltzmann-population.name: Boltzmann Population Ratio
boltzmann-population.intro: Enter the two-level energy gap ΔE (eV) and absolute temperature T; compute the high-to-low level particle ratio N₂/N₁ = exp(−ΔE/kT to understand how higher temperature increases upper-level occupancy.

compton-shift.name: Compton Shift
compton-shift.intro: Compute the Compton wavelength shift of X-rays scattered by an electron as a function of scattering angle, for Compton-effect and photon-electron interaction analysis.

compton-wavelength.name: Compton Wavelength
compton-wavelength.intro: Compute a particle's Compton wavelength λ_c = h/(mc) from its mass, output in wavelength units, useful for particle physics and quantum-effect study.

cyclotron-frequency.name: Cyclotron Frequency
cyclotron-frequency.intro: Compute the cyclotron angular frequency ω = qB/m of a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field, useful for cyclotrons, plasma physics and particle-motion analysis.

de-broglie-wavelength.name: de Broglie Wavelength
de-broglie-wavelength.intro: Compute the matter-wave wavelength λ = h/p from momentum p, useful for electron-microscope, quantum-mechanics and wave-particle duality wavelength estimates.

energy-time-uncertainty.name: Energy-Time Uncertainty
energy-time-uncertainty.intro: Enter the time uncertainty Δt of a particle's existence and compute the minimum energy broadening ΔE ≥ ℏ/(2Δt), showing shorter-lived states have broader levels, for excited-state and natural-linewidth estimates.

fermi-energy-3d.name: 3D Fermi Energy
fermi-energy-3d.intro: Enter the free-electron density n and effective mass m; compute the Fermi energy E_F = (ℏ²/2m)(3π²n)^{2/3} for estimating the highest occupied level in metals and semiconductors.

heisenberg-uncertainty.name: Heisenberg Uncertainty
heisenberg-uncertainty.intro: Compute the lower bound of the position-momentum uncertainty product Δx·Δp ≥ ħ/2, for quantum-mechanics principle demos and measurement-limit discussions.

hydrogen-energy-level.name: Hydrogen Energy Level
hydrogen-energy-level.intro: Compute the energy E_n = −13.6/n² eV of the n-th hydrogen level, for Bohr-model, spectrum and atomic-physics level and transition analysis.

infinite-well-energy.name: Infinite Square Well Energy
infinite-well-energy.intro: Compute the discrete energy levels E_n of a particle in a 1D infinite square well from well width and mass, for quantum-mechanics stationary-state problems and teaching demos.

mass-energy-equivalence.name: Mass-Energy Equivalence (E=mc²)
mass-energy-equivalence.intro: Online E=mc² calculator: enter a mass to get the equivalent energy, or reverse from energy to mass, for nuclear and relativistic teaching (client-side).

pair-production-threshold.name: Pair-Production Threshold
pair-production-threshold.intro: Compute the minimum photon energy (≥ 2m_e c²) required to produce an electron-positron pair, for high-energy physics and gamma-ray matter-interaction analysis.

photoelectric-effect.name: Photoelectric Effect
photoelectric-effect.intro: Enter incident light frequency (or wavelength) and metal work function; compute the maximum photoelectron kinetic energy via Einstein's equation, judge whether emission occurs and give the cutoff frequency, for photocell and PV principle demos.

photoelectric-threshold.name: Photoelectric Threshold Frequency (f₀ = φ/h)
photoelectric-threshold.intro: Compute the photoelectric cutoff frequency f₀ = φ/h from the metal work function φ (eV), for photoelectric-effect and quantum-physics exercises.

photon-energy.name: Photon Energy
photon-energy.intro: Compute photon energy E = hν = hc/λ from frequency or wavelength, for single-photon energy conversion in optics, atomic physics and photodetection.

photon-flux.name: Photon Flux
photon-flux.intro: Enter optical power P and wavelength λ; compute the photons per second (photon flux) N = P·λ/(hc), for comparing single-photon flux of different wavelengths in optical detection and quantum-source estimates.

photon-momentum.name: Photon Momentum
photon-momentum.intro: Compute a photon's relativistic momentum p = h/λ from wavelength, for radiation pressure, Compton scattering and quantum-optics momentum estimates.

quantum-oscillator-energy.name: Quantum Harmonic Oscillator Energy
quantum-oscillator-energy.intro: Enter oscillator quantum number n and frequency f; compute the energy E_n = ℏω(n+½), demonstrating equally spaced levels with zero-point energy, for molecular vibration and phonon analysis.

rydberg-wavelength.name: Rydberg Wavelength
rydberg-wavelength.intro: Compute the hydrogen spectral-line wavelength from initial and final levels and the Rydberg constant, for Balmer-series emission/absorption wavelength estimates.

spin-magnetic-moment.name: Spin Magnetic Moment (μ = μ_B·m_l)
spin-magnetic-moment.intro: Enter the orbital magnetic quantum number m_l; compute the orbital magnetic moment μ = μ_B·m_l (in Bohr magnetons μ_B), illustrating orientation moments for atomic magnetism and Zeeman effect.

stefan-boltzmann-power.name: Stefan-Boltzmann Power (P = σ·A·T⁴)
stefan-boltzmann-power.intro: Enter blackbody surface area A and absolute temperature T; compute total radiated power P = σ·A·T⁴, showing radiation rising sharply with temperature, for stars, heaters and thermal-radiation estimates.

thermal-de-broglie.name: Thermal de Broglie Wavelength
thermal-de-broglie.intro: Enter particle mass m and temperature T; compute the thermal de Broglie wavelength λ = h/√(2πmkT) to judge when a gas becomes quantum-degenerate, for Bose-Einstein condensation analysis.

wien-displacement.name: Wien's Displacement Law
wien-displacement.intro: Compute the inverse relation between blackbody peak wavelength and temperature λ_max·T = b, for thermal radiation, stellar temperature estimates and infrared physics study.

zeeman-splitting.name: Zeeman Splitting (ΔE = μ_B·B)
zeeman-splitting.intro: Enter magnetic flux density B; compute the energy gap ΔE = μ_B·B between adjacent Zeeman sublevels, showing equally spaced splitting under an external field, for atomic-spectrum Zeeman effect and field calibration.
